description: This bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance measured by MAP@10 for two distinct sampling strategies—“Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” (purple bars) and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (yellow bars)—across five different values of the parameter m, which are labeled 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled “MAP@10”, is scaled linearly from 23.0 to 27.0, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.5. For each value of m, there are two adjacent bars representing the respective sampling strategies. The purple bars, corresponding to the Fine-to-Coarse strategy, are consistently taller than the yellow bars for the Uniform strategy across all m values. Specifically, for m=6, the purple bar reaches approximately 25.9 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.4; for m=7, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.7 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.8; for m=8, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.3 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.9; for m=9, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.6 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 25.2; and for m=10, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.4 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.4. The bars are not sorted by height; instead, they are grouped by m value, with the Fine-to-Coarse strategy bars appearing to the left of the Uniform strategy bars for each m. The chart includes a legend in the top right corner that distinguishes the two strategies by color. There are no visual annotations or emphasis on specific bars beyond their color-coded representation.
